limitations: Calibration subset; full coverage and human review pending.

substantive_analysis.title: Building Trust to Solve Commons Dilemmas: Taking Small Steps to Test an Evolving Theory of Collective Action
substantive_analysis.publication_identity: Working paper W08–23, 22 September 2008; forthcoming in Games, Groups, and the Global Good; SSRN 1304695
substantive_analysis.supplied_version: Original-author working paper, 39 pages, with figures at end
substantive_analysis.edition_relation: Syllabus names the 2009 chapter, pp. 207–228. The supplied 2008 working paper is directly inspected; chapter equivalence is unverified.
substantive_analysis.source_bound_claim: Ostrom argues that cooperation depends on context, including norms, information, communication, monitoring and sanctions; no single variable has the same effect in every setting.
substantive_analysis.source_locator: PDF pp. 7, 21–26; monitoring and graduated sanctions on p. 25

argument_steps.label: Puzzle
argument_steps.statement: Cooperation varies even in simplified dilemmas; context changes the effects of communication, group attributes and property rights.

argument_steps.label: Mechanism
argument_steps.statement: Trust and reciprocity connect expectations about others to willingness to cooperate; monitoring and sanctions must be assessed in their setting.

argument_steps.label: Conditional use
argument_steps.statement: Use only where the case records support a cooperation mechanism. Litigation withdrawal is not evidence of trust or representative consent.
argument_steps.locator_or_basis: Study limitation, not a Chilean empirical finding

substantive_analysis.permitted_use: Use only if actual case evidence concerns cooperation, reciprocity, monitoring or asymmetric access.
substantive_analysis.prohibited_inference: Do not infer community trust from withdrawal, or transplant a commons design prescription into Chilean permitting.
qualifications: Asymmetric power is identified as an important further experimental task, pp. 23–24.
The cited studies are summarized by Ostrom, not independently revalidated here.
substantive_analysis.missing_dependency: Human source-fidelity and assignment-fit review; original Cerrillos instruments for any case-specific claim
substantive_analysis.case_application_status: proposed analytical use; not a case finding
